entries.behavior_changes: Preserve bounded ordered bootstrap buffering, ACK-gated chunked writes, deadlines, close semantics, and synchronous bootstrap payload tagging. Add a locked NextSeq accessor so the association can freeze the exact receive ownership boundary for prepare/detach; no payload-byte mode guessing is introduced.
entries.tests: internal/faketcp/bootstrap_stream_test.go covers reordering, per-chunk ACK gating, deadlines, chunk/byte bounds, uint32 sequence wrap, marker scope, and close/EOF; association tests use NextSeq as the transition boundary.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract wrap-aware seqLT/seqLE only. No Receiver, SACK/RACK, repair pressure, or steady-state delivery policy is migrated here.
entries.tests: bootstrap and transition tests exercise comparisons across uint32 wrap.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only copied Pending payload ownership, cumulative ACK release, ACK waiting, oldest-payload RTO retransmit, bootstrap 2s retransmit ceiling, and the invariant that bootstrap retries do not back off the shared RTO. The archived bootstrap_retransmit_test.go was also inspected as behavioral evidence. Steady-state SACK/RACK/repair-budget/partial-reliability logic is intentionally not migrated.
entries.tests: internal/faketcp/bootstrap_sender_test.go covers the archived bootstrap ceiling invariant, later ordinary RTO backoff, cumulative ACK wait/deadline, retransmit Seq/payload identity, and uint32 wrap.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract IPv4/TCP handshake/bootstrap build+parse, checksum and SYN option handling. WBD fixed MSS/SACK/window-scale remains a client presentation helper only; server initial-SYN validity is independent of that fingerprint. MarshalSegment now serializes the Segment's negotiated SYN options so ordinary peers can omit SACK/WS or advertise different values. Steady-state SACK blocks remain deferred.
entries.tests: packet_test.go keeps fixed WBD/Windows persona checks; syn_compat_test.go covers ordinary legal SYN combinations, negotiated SYN-ACK option serialization and malformed initial SYN rejection.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve presentation-only legacy/windows11 persona selection while moving the actual SYN rewrite into the extracted packet builder. No sequence/reliability behavior depends on persona.
entries.tests: internal/faketcp/packet_test.go fixes the Windows TTL/DF/SYN option ordering/checksum shape and proves the explicit legacy persona remains byte-identical to the base builder.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve non-Windows default legacy persona.
entries.tests: Cross-platform Actions compile and run packet tests; explicit legacy persona wire identity is covered in packet_test.go.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve Windows default windows11 packet persona.
entries.tests: Windows Actions compile/run the package; packet_test.go explicitly validates windows11 SYN presentation.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract ServerFlow, bounded association table, SYN/SYN-ACK/final-ACK, shared sequence space, bootstrap sender and transition routing. Audit closure separates legal TCP admission from WBD identity: any valid initial SYN is accepted, peer MSS/WS/SACK are recorded, missing IPv4 MSS defaults to 536, bootstrap chunking is capped by peer MSS, and SYN-ACK WS/SACK are offered only when negotiated. Steady-state Receiver/SACK/RACK/FEC remain deferred.
entries.tests: internal/faketcp/association_test.go covers WBD SYN admission, cross-flow isolation, data-bearing final ACK delivery, real BootstrapStream Write -> Sender WaitAck -> incoming ACK unblock, exact transition boundary, early-record queue/detach, pure ACK ownership, table duplicate/cap behavior, same-association final-bootstrap payload loss retransmit with identical Seq/payload, ACK-loss retransmit without duplicate peer delivery, and a dropped first new-mode record whose successor still routes immediately; the successor is opened by tlsrecord at PN=1 to prove no HOL at the handoff. syn_compat_test.go additionally covers ordinary MSS/WS/SACK/no-option profiles and peer-MSS bootstrap sizing.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract the REALITY-like HMAC SessionID route marker, exact ClientHello identity parsing, replay connection and name normalization only. Ticket/auth/fallback dialing code is not migrated in this atomic task.
entries.tests: internal/realityfront/tls_test.go validates the route marker on the pinned Firefox120 ClientHello and recognized/unrecognized classification behavior.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only bounded TLS ClientHello record reading plus SNI/ALPN parsing so classification can retain byte-exact raw hello for later fallback or replay. Target dialing, bidirectional splice and transfer limits remain deferred.
entries.tests: internal/realityfront/tls_test.go verifies an unrecognized hello retains raw bytes and SNI for later fallback rather than being consumed irreversibly.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve the pinned uTLS Firefox120 ClientHello persona and same-connection crypto/tls server takeover, but remove username/password/ticket coupling from this atomic layer. Exporter keys are derived directly from the original uTLS/crypto-tls ConnectionState using WIRE_SPEC context; the old hand-copy into tls.ConnectionState is deliberately not reused. uTLS v1.6.5 Firefox120 couples renegotiation_info to RenegotiateOnceAsClient, which disables exporter access, so the extracted client keeps the renegotiation_info extension bytes/order but changes only its internal acceptance policy to RenegotiateNever before the final BuildHandshakeState.
entries.tests: internal/realityfront/tls_test.go compares Firefox120 preset fields and performs real TLS 1.3 over ServerAssociation.BootstrapConn, requiring client/server exporter-derived tlsrecord KeyPair equality, context binding, and early-record prepare/detach preservation. internal/realityfront/renegotiation_test.go additionally proves the Firefox120 renegotiation_info extension stays byte-identical while its internal policy is RenegotiateNever.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only one protected TLS application request carrying username/password, bounded length parsing, and constant-time credential comparison. Replace archived ticket issuance with the new P2 admission response required by WIRE_SPEC: record_version=1, exact 16-byte TunnelID, client/server record wire limits, and a server-generated 16-byte incarnation nonce. Unknown versions are explicitly rejected. No ticket filesystem, lease provider, installation ID, CLI, or fallback dialing code is migrated. Audit closure adds one absolute candidate establishment deadline spanning TLS plus protected admission through final-reply ACK/detach; context cancellation wakes blocked I/O, failure closes the candidate association/connection, and only successful handoff clears the deadline.
entries.tests: internal/realityfront/admission_test.go covers successful protected admission over the real uTLS/crypto-tls FakeTCP association, server-generated nonce and parameter echo, exporter key equality from negotiated context, prepare-before-final-reply ordering, detached transition state, authentication failure without prepare, unknown-version rejection, TunnelID/context mismatch rejection, and record-limit bounds. audit_closure_test.go covers post-TLS silence, partial admission, context cancellation, unacknowledged final reply abort, and deadline clearing after success.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only the post-classification decoy continuation: validate the already-parsed SNI, dial one fixed target, replay the exact already-consumed raw ClientHello before any splice bytes, then bidirectionally copy on the same inbound FakeTCP BootstrapConn with bounded optional per-direction bytes and session deadline. The single HandleServerAssociation consumes one ClientHello once: recognized WBD enters protected admission and never dials fallback; unrecognized enters decoy fallback and never prepares the record transition. Splice shutdown attempts TCP half-close when available and otherwise full Close; close-race errors io.ErrClosedPipe, net.ErrClosed, faketcp.ErrBootstrapClosed, ECONNRESET and EPIPE are treated as benign termination. Observer/demo witness logic is not migrated. HandleServerAssociation now applies the same absolute WBD candidate deadline during ClientHello classification and recognized admission; once classified as an ordinary visitor, that candidate deadline is cleared and fallback's own bounded session policy takes over.
entries.tests: internal/realityfront/fallback_test.go covers byte-identical raw ClientHello replay into a real TLS decoy, application response on the same client association, final decoy TLS close_notify being drained/ACKed by the in-memory FakeTCP peer after application Close (matching kernel TCP ACK behavior), bounded splice termination, no transition prepare on fallback, recognized WBD with zero fallback dials, and SNI mismatch rejection before dialing. audit_closure_test.go proves non-WBD ordinary SYN profiles reach fallback classification without using the WBD SYN fingerprint.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Preserve WBDLFRG1 20-byte LINK fragment wire, non-zero uint32 PacketID identity, 65535-byte original datagram limit, out-of-order completion, identical-duplicate idempotence, conflicting duplicate/metadata rejection, 16 incomplete assemblies, 5s assembly TTL, 64 retired IDs and 10s retired TTL. Remove the archived dependency on internal/fec error sentinels and all Path/FEC runtime coupling. Reassembly storage is sparse instead of allocating declared fragment_count up front; add explicit buffered fragment/payload bounds and an owner-callable Expire method so idle traffic can still retire incomplete datagrams.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/datagram_fragment_test.go fixes exact wire fields, PacketID increment/wrap and reserved-magic escape; covers normal/out-of-order reassembly, identical duplicates, conflicting duplicates without replacing first arrival, explicit idle expiry, max fragment-count metadata without preallocation, entry/byte/assembly/retired bounds, malformed/oversize isolation, and the P3 no-HOL case where datagram A permanently misses one fragment while later complete datagram B is delivered first.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve live FEC v1 constants, 56-byte WF header, systematic 20+20 generator/GF(256) math, and the authoritative parity byte. Export the exact archived live fixed set 20:4/8/10/12/16/20 for the new path; tighten reserved header byte 3 to zero. FEC off remains a LINK/path mode rather than an RS geometry.
entries.tests: internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go fixes the exact supported matrix, rejects non-live geometries, checks byte-level streaming v1 headers for every profile, and cross-checks fast 20:20 parity against the reference codec.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve the qualified fast systematic 20+20 codec and shared GF multiply table. The live v1 encoder continues to compute the same generator and transmits only the negotiated first R parity rows; no profile-v2 codec/wire is introduced.
entries.tests: internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go exercises recovery for every live R and compares fast parity against the reference implementation.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve immediate systematic source emission, immutable BlockID/shard identity, full-block R parity, and partial-block min(dataCount,R) parity so short blocks do not expand to N+20. Returned low-level slices retain the archived borrowed-slot contract; internal/linkdata/fec_path.go adds the owned-copy product boundary.
entries.tests: internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go covers systematic first-arrival, all six parity counts, full recovery and partial-block parity counts; internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go covers cross-20-source ownership and LINK integration.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve bounded heavy decoder state, immediate first-delivery of streaming sources, known-zero partial-block semantics, compact retired fallback and late systematic delivery. Add explicit active conflicting-duplicate payload rejection (ErrShardMismatch) instead of silently accepting a different payload for an already-present shard; identical duplicates remain idempotent.
entries.tests: internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go covers every fixed profile, cross-block no-HOL under maxBlocks pressure, identical/conflicting duplicates, profile mismatch isolation and bounded retired state.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve compact contiguous completed-BlockID history and out-of-order range merging; no expected-BlockID receive window is added.
entries.tests: internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go covers long sequential completion compaction.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve RetireRecoveryExpired: release heavy parity/reconstruction payload while retaining compact exact first-delivery state so late systematic sources remain deliverable once.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go drives idle 3-second expiry and verifies late systematic first-arrival/duplicate behavior.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve constant-time decoder pressure counters and detailed bounded-state diagnostics used by the new LINK/FEC path tests; no global/shared decoder is introduced.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go asserts heavy/retired state around pressure and expiry.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract the 3-second absolute FEC recovery deadline tracker and adapt it to an explicit owner-callable Expire method. Progress and duplicates do not refresh the deadline; expiry can run with zero inbound traffic.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go covers absolute non-refreshing deadline, idle expiry, compact retirement and late first-arrival.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only LINK-fragment -> lane-local FEC -> LINK-reassembly ordering and the archived live fixed profile behavior. Remove control/runtime/statistics coupling, DTLS wording and FEC observer plumbing. The adapter returns owned wire copies so a single datagram spanning multiple 20-source blocks cannot be corrupted by encoder backing-slot reuse.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go covers off plus all six fixed profiles, systematic delivery before parity flush, missing-fragment recovery, malformed-input isolation, lane-local state and a large datagram crossing an FEC block boundary.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only the authoritative archived live fixed FEC policy set: off and TailRS 20:4/8/10/12/16/20. Startup/auth/control state is not migrated in this P3 atom; non-live 20:9 and causal/profile-v2 choices remain unsupported.
entries.tests: internal/linkdata/fec_path_test.go fixes the exact public profile list; internal/fec/fec_profiles_test.go rejects non-live parity values.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Preserve one operator-visible connection MTU range 576..9000 and nested-budget fail-closed behavior. Remove old control/gamepath coupling, fixed 40-byte carrier assumption and DTLS13RecordReserve=32. New budget takes actual IPv4/TCP header lengths, optional smaller local packet ceiling, peer MSS with IPv4 missing-MSS fallback 536, protected-admission record wire limit, and the live fixed FEC profile. It then derives record wire/payload, FEC/LINK frame and WBDLFRG1 fragment payload using active tlsrecord 31-byte, FEC v1 56-byte and LINK 20-byte overheads. No hidden 1360/1400/1500 cap is retained.
entries.tests: internal/pathmtu/budget_test.go covers required outer MTUs 576/1280/1400/1500/1600/9000 with FEC off/on, every live fixed FEC profile, advertised/missing peer MSS, actual TCP option header length, local packet ceiling, negotiated record limit and fail-closed invalid/negative-capacity cases. internal/pathmtu/integration_test.go feeds derived LinkFrameMTU into active linkdata FEC paths and seals resulting datagrams with tlsrecord, proving FEC wire <= record payload, record <= peer MSS/negotiated limit and serialized IPv4 packet <= effective outer MTU without a hidden clamp.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Preserve per-session/lane owned path state, per-lane serialization, immutable activation parameters, returned wire ownership and close isolation. Rewrite the old account/peer registry and DTLS/control LinkConfig coupling into a single lane owner over active pathmtu + linkdata + tlsrecord. FEC off and 20:4/8/10/12/16/20 are immutable per incarnation; direction-specific admission limits and C2S/S2C keys are pinned at construction; config/profile mismatch fails before activation. No account registry, socket adapter, Tunnel/Game or CLI is migrated.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/lane_test.go covers all fixed profiles plus off in both directions, immutable profile/record-limit mismatch rejection, admission/server peer-MSS direction binding, record-PN out-of-order delivery, dropped-A/later-B no-HOL for every profile, owner-driven idle FEC expiry and late systematic first-arrival, detached transition payload handoff without TCP-seq ordering, immutable returned record wire across later encoder reuse, close isolation and concurrent per-lane PN serialization under race.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only the post-admission ownership handoff shape: bind one authenticated association to one immutable lane configuration and consume copied transition payloads after detach. The new server adapter reads existing realityfront AdmissionResult plus faketcp PeerTCPProfile without changing P2 interfaces; server TX uses ClientLimit/S2C and peer advertised MSS, server RX uses ServerLimit/C2S and the server-advertised IPv4 MSS. TCP Seq is not converted into record ordering.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/lane_test.go verifies server admission direction limits/MSS/profile binding and that detached transition records are delivered by record PN/FEC/LINK semantics rather than TCP Seq ordering.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Extract only the product transport cardinality policy: 1..4 authoritative logical lanes, six retiring/transition headroom incarnations, and ten total concurrent physical incarnations. Lease manager, installation allocation, source anti-spoof, CLI and platform state are deliberately not migrated in this atomic task.
entries.tests: internal/logicaltunnel/lifecycle_test.go fixes the 1..4 policy and fifth-lane rejection; internal/datapath/tunnel_owner_test.go separately enforces six transition headroom and ten total physical incarnations.

entries.behavior_changes: Preserve lane membership refs, monotonic generation fencing, same-ID promotion, candidate/draining lifecycle primitives, and DORMANT clearing of transport membership while retaining desired wake policy. The extracted lifecycle owns no FakeTCP, TLS-like record, LINK, FEC, socket or Game wire state.
entries.tests: internal/logicaltunnel/lifecycle_test.go covers desired cardinality, same-ID generation advance with one logical lane, stale-generation rejection, and DORMANT followed by a fresh wake generation.

entries.behavior_changes: Adapt the archived logical membership/generation model into a bounded coordinator over already-created internal/datapath Lane incarnations. Business flows are bounded logical registrations and never create or close a lane; Normal flows resolve the existing lane 1 at send time. Same-ID candidate promotion moves the prior Lane into bounded retirement, stale completions are fenced, candidate failure preserves the old lane, and DORMANT closes transport incarnations while preserving flow registrations for wake. Game PacketID/racing, lane creation, padding policy and FEC internals are not reimplemented.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/tunnel_owner_test.go covers multiple sibling flows sharing one Normal lane, flow-close isolation, bounded registry/no lane growth, same-ID replacement and late-old generation discard, candidate failure, DORMANT/wake, immutable per-incarnation FEC profiles, 1..4 logical lanes, six transition headroom, ten physical-incarnation bound, default padding off, and concurrent shared-lane PN serialization under the Actions race job.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Extract stable Account+Installation -> Logical Tunnel identity and deterministic IPv4 /32 lease allocation, while adapting active TunnelID representation from archived hex-string storage to an exact 16-byte value that round-trips to hex and directly matches the protected-admission wire. Preserve same-active-identity reacquire, distinct installation/account isolation, route cloning/canonicalization, bounded pool exhaustion and release semantics. Do not migrate old dataplane source validator, raw-IP gateway, CLI, TUN, netns or platform runtime in this atom.
entries.tests: internal/logicaltunnel/identity_test.go covers raw 16-byte TunnelID/admission round-trip, same installation stable TunnelID/lease, same-account different-installation and different-account same-installation isolation, concurrent reacquire without fork, release/address reuse with fresh TunnelID, owned route copies and fail-closed pool/identity validation.

entries.behavior_changes: Bind the already-extracted TunnelOwner to one stable logicaltunnel.Lease before any Lane incarnation is admitted. The owner retains an owned lease copy across same-ID replacement, retirement, DORMANT and wake; BusinessFlow lifecycle remains independent and still reuses existing lanes. Unleased owner construction is retained only for lower-level tests/adapters.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/tunnel_identity_test.go proves replacement and DORMANT/wake preserve TunnelID/lease, existing flows resume on the wake incarnation, and another installation's lane is rejected before membership mutation.

entries.behavior_changes: Add the minimal protected-admission bridge: require the admission's exact 16-byte TunnelID to equal the Manager-issued lease TunnelID before constructing the server LaneConfig. This does not change the P2 admission wire, credentials, exporter context, FakeTCP transition or lane crypto ownership.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/tunnel_identity_test.go constructs admission handoff for two isolated installations, requires cross-installation TunnelID rejection, then proves the matching Manager lease creates a Lane accepted by the leased TunnelOwner.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Extract only the Logical Tunnel IPv4 source anti-spoof semantic without importing the archived dataplane package: require one well-formed IPv4 packet, archived 9000-byte product ceiling, valid IHL/total-length, and source exactly equal to the /32 lease. IPv6, another lease source and malformed packets fail closed. No raw-IP metadata, gateway, TUN, netns or platform runtime is migrated.
entries.tests: internal/logicaltunnel/source_test.go covers exact/mapped lease acceptance, other-lease and IPv6 rejection, invalid lease, short/bad-IHL/length-mismatch and oversize malformed packets.

entries.behavior_changes: Adapt the archived client TUN source-fence placement to the active leased TunnelOwner: RoleClient BusinessFlow.Outbound validates the inner IPv4 source before Lane.Outbound, so rejected packets cannot consume PN, LINK/FEC state or padding/record state. Apply only to leased owners; unleased lower-level owner tests/adapters retain their previous generic-datagram behavior. Do not migrate the old TUN bridge, split engine, CLI or logging.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/tunnel_source_test.go proves spoofed/non-IPv4/malformed leased-client packets fail before lane state/PN mutation, a sibling valid BusinessFlow still uses PN=0, and client receive of server-to-client internet-source packets remains allowed.

entries.behavior_changes: Adapt only the archived server-side post-decode source==lease fence into TunnelOwner.InboundPayload. The owner first validates the authoritative lane generation, decodes through the existing Lane, generation-fences completion, then on RoleServer leased owners drops each decoded inner datagram whose IPv4 source is not the lease and reports the error via PathErrors/SourceDiscards. Old raw-IP metadata, per-session netns/TUN and NAT runtime are not migrated.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/tunnel_source_test.go sends a forged packet directly through a client Lane to bypass the client owner and proves the leased server owner drops it after decrypt/FEC/LINK decode; valid leased traffic is delivered and a retired generation is rejected before business delivery.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Extract only the WGL1 Game data envelope and tunnel-wide PacketID first-arrival dedupe semantics: 32-byte header, 16-byte SessionID, uint64 PacketID, lane-distinct copies, 1..4 encoded LaneIDs, bounded replay state, duplicate suppression and out-of-order unique delivery without expected-ID HOL. Add the archived product default replay window 4096 as an active constant. Local UDP control, membership wire, pacer and subprocess runtime are not migrated.
entries.tests: internal/gamelane/gamelane_test.go covers one PacketID across four lane-distinct envelopes, first-arrival delivery with later lane copies deduplicated, out-of-order unique PacketIDs without HOL, bounded replay/stale rejection, wrong-session and invalid-lane/reserved-byte fail-closed behavior.

entries.behavior_changes: Adapt only the archived client race fan-out into the single-process TunnelOwner. GameOutbound allocates one tunnel-wide PacketID and sends a lane-distinct copy through every currently authoritative Lane; candidate/retiring incarnations do not create a second PacketID namespace. Each Lane retains independent LINK/FEC/record state. Leased client IPv4 source validation happens before PacketID allocation or Lane mutation. No UDP loopback process, control socket, pacer, CLI or lane-address registry is migrated.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/game_owner_test.go covers 3-lane same-PacketID fan-out, one Lane outbound datagram per authoritative lane, first-arrival racing, unique PacketID out-of-order delivery, client source rejection before PacketID allocation, business-flow growth without lane growth, and PacketID continuity across same-ID replacement plus DORMANT/wake.

entries.behavior_changes: Adapt the archived server shared Game decoder into the active owner boundary. Game SessionID is the exact stable 16-byte TunnelID; inbound work is generation-fenced, Game envelope LaneID must match the authoritative transport LaneRef, and leased server source validation is performed on the inner IPv4 packet before committing PacketID dedupe so an invalid first copy cannot suppress a later valid copy. Duplicate/stale state is tunnel-wide while FEC remains lane-local. Old rawip metadata, UDP service bridge, membership sockets and session subprocess lifecycle are not migrated.
entries.tests: internal/datapath/game_owner_test.go proves lane3-first delivery with lane1/lane2 duplicate suppression, spoofed source and wrong-LaneID copies do not poison the same PacketID, reverse server-to-client internet-source packets remain valid, and Game statistics expose logical sends/copies/delivery/duplicate/mismatch counts.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Extract the final shared-root-TUN lease demultiplexing semantic but remove the old localhost UDP/rawipbackend metadata bridge and process/session peer registry. Active registration binds an already-admitted leased TunnelOwner directly by stable TunnelID+/32; exact runtime rebind gets a fresh token and stale owners are fenced. Shared-TUN return packets demux by IPv4 destination lease to Normal/Game owner APIs; owner-decoded client egress is source==lease checked again before TUN write. The superseded per-session netns/veth/double-NAT gateway path is explicitly not migrated.
entries.tests: internal/linuxserver/router_test.go covers two independent leases, Normal/Game destination demux, duplicate lease/tunnel rejection, exact identity rebind with stale-token fencing, source-spoof rejection, malformed IPv4/no-route/short-TUN-write fail-closed behavior and independent unregister.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract only ownership semantics into a structured non-executing plan: one shared TUN route for the lease pool, saved/restored ip_forward and TUN rp_filter sysctls, WBD-marked outbound/established-return FORWARD rules and one host MASQUERADE rule. No global ruleset flush/restore, no per-session NAT operation. Server host DNS is deliberately unchanged; DNS packets are ordinary tunneled IPv4. The later privileged runtime executor must materialize and clean only these owned objects.
entries.tests: internal/linuxserver/network_plan_test.go verifies exact route/setup/teardown, saved sysctl intent, three WBD markers, DNS unchanged, nft forward-chain validation and fail-closed invalid TUN/prefix/MTU/backend inputs.

entries.behavior_changes: Extract the minimal Linux shared-TUN device primitive only: /dev/net/tun, IFF_TUN|IFF_NO_PI, bounded interface name, ReadPacket/WritePacket/Close. No archived UDP/framed bridge or platform subprocess orchestration is migrated. A !linux stub reports unsupported so Windows repository builds remain explicit.
entries.tests: Linux/Windows Actions compile the platform-specific files through package enumeration; shared-TUN packet semantics are tested against the PacketWriter adapter without requiring root/CAP_NET_ADMIN. Real privileged TUN execution remains a later platform qualification gate.

entries.behavior_changes: Archive source SHA b5c848f4e9afdffd15d1bc451560edf4e9390a35. Materialize the previously extracted shared-TUN ownership semantics as an in-process privileged executor: snapshot/restore ip_forward and TUN rp_filter, apply/cleanup only the lease route and three WBD-marked forwarding/NAT rules, and leave existing firewall policy/rules intact. iptables cleanup deletes exact comment-tagged rules; nft uses a dedicated WBD NAT table and deletes only WBD marker handles from an explicitly selected existing forward chain. If nft sees an unknown forward hook without an explicit chain, it fails closed rather than guessing. No per-user netns/veth/double NAT is restored.
entries.tests: internal/linuxserver/runtime_privileged_linux_test.go plus next-foundation p4-linux-shared-tun-privileged matrix exercise real /dev/net/tun, route/sysctl/firewall apply and cleanup under isolated root network namespaces for both iptables and nft, preserving a pre-existing DROP forward policy.

The gate distinguishes real privileged TUN/netfilter execution from ordinary hosted unit tests.

Remove all old process/controller coupling. A !windows stub is explicit unsupported.

Extract the route ownership model into a pure active plan: lease must be IPv4 /32; server underlay /32 is pinned to an already-observed physical interface/next-hop before broad capture; optional direct prefixes stay on that physical path; full IPv4 capture is the two /1 routes; DNS resolver /32s are captured and ordinary DNS uses one WBD-owned NRPT namespace='.' rule.
